title: Bridging Performance Portability and Scalability for Plasma Simulations on Heterogeneous Systems
problem: Achieving both portability (run on CPUs and GPUs) and scalability (high performance on each) is challenging due to abstraction overhead; performance portability abstractions like Kokkos can hide hardware capabilities.
motivation: VPIC (Vector Particle-In-Cell) code requires extensive platform-specific optimizations; abstraction layers (Kokkos) enable portability but can introduce performance overhead.
method: VPIC 2.0 adopts Kokkos for portability, then mitigates overhead via: (1) enhanced vectorization, (2) platform-targeted particle sorting, (3) optimized memory access patterns.
key_novelty: First demonstration that Kokkos-based particle-in-cell code can match hand-tuned performance on CPUs while achieving superlinear scaling on GPUs.
contributions: VPIC 2.0 with Kokkos for performance portability
Particle sorting optimization targeting specific platforms
limitations: Abstract-only; lacks specific speedup numbers, GPU scaling curves, or comparison on multiple architectures
